diagnostic_evidence.quote: A strictly monotonically increasing and differentiable function $\sigma: \R \to \R$ is called \emph{sigmoidal} if it satisfies

issues.failure_explanation: Definition def:sigm_act (eq:sigm_act) requires lim_{t->-inf} sigma(t) = 0 and lim_{t->+inf} sigma(t) = 1. But tanh(t) -> -1 and arctan(t) -> -pi/2 as t -> -infty, so neither tanh nor arctan is sigmoidal as defined. The claim that they are sigmoidal is false, and the approximation theorems (which assume a (bounded) sigmoidal activation) therefore do not cover these standard activation functions as the text asserts.

failure_location.quote: For examples, the logistic sigmoid function, the hyperbolic tangens and the arctangens are sigmoidial.

issues.overall_effect: The admissible activation class is misstated; the named activation functions fall outside the hypotheses of the paper's approximation results unless the definition is rescaled.
issues.title: tanh and arctan do not satisfy the paper's definition of sigmoidal
issues.why_classification: A purely local definitional reformulation restores the intended examples; every substantive claim, rate and guarantee survives unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The proof follow easily from the Rellich-Kondrachov theorem (see \cite[Theorem 6.2]{Ada75}), which states that the embedding $H^s(\Omega_\X) \hookrightarrow C(\overline{\Omega_\X})$ is compact for $s > \frac{m}{2}$, and from \cite[Theorem 4 \& Theorem 5]{TiaHon95}.
be a continuous operator with respect to the $(H^s(\Omega_\X),\norms{\cdot}_{H^s})$-topology, and assume that the domain $\dom{F}$ is compact in $C(\overline{\Omega_\X})$.

issues.failure_explanation: The invoked theorems of Tian-Hong/Chen-Chen require continuity of F with respect to the topology in which the domain is compact (the sup-norm); H^s-continuity does not imply sup-norm continuity, so [TiaHon95, Thm 4 & 5] is applied outside its hypotheses. The statements are in fact false: take dom(F) = the closed unit ball of H^s(Omega_X), which is compact in C(overline{Omega_X}) (bounded H^s-balls are equicontinuous and the H^s-ball is closed in C), and F[x] = <x,g>_{H^s} * phi(t) with phi not identically 0 and g not a finite linear combination of Riesz representers of point evaluations. F is H^s-continuous, but every F_n from eq:deeponet depends on x only through finitely many sample values; choosing h in the joint kernel of all sample functionals with <h,g>_{H^s} = 1 gives F_n[x+h] = F_n[x] while F[x+h] - F[x] = phi, so the asserted uniform error < epsilon is impossible for epsilon < ||phi||_{L^2}/2.

failure_location.quote: be a continuous functional with respect to the $(H^s(\Omega_\X),\norms{\cdot}_{H^s})$-topology, and suppose that the domain $\dom{F}$ is compact in $C(\overline{\Omega_\X})$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restore the original hypothesis (F continuous with respect to the C(overline{Omega_X})-topology on the compact domain); the H^s-setting then enters only through Rellich-Kondrachov compactness. The H^s-continuity hypothesis must be dropped, so the claimed generalization is abandoned.
issues.overall_effect: Both restated universal approximation theorems for Sobolev-space data (th:functional apx, th:operatorapx) are false; the abstract's claim of extending neural-operator approximation beyond spaces of continuous functions is unsupported, and the proof of thm:l2 operator apx, which invokes th:operatorapx, loses its licence.
issues.title: Restated universal approximation theorems in Sobolev spaces are false
issues.why_classification: The stated theorems admit concrete counterexamples; every sound resolution removes the claimed Sobolev-topology regime, so the section's advertised contribution is abandoned rather than locally repaired.

issues.failure_explanation: With the zero extension fixed in Definition def:mollifier, item (v) is false: whenever x has a non-vanishing trace, mollification creates a boundary layer of width ~xi and height O(1). Concretely, x = 1 on (0,1) (in H^k for all k) gives x_xi(s) = int_0^1 phi_xi(s-t) dt, which differs from 1 on a set of measure ~xi, so ||x_xi - x||_{L^2(0,1)} is of order xi^{1/2}, not C xi^{k-s} for k-s >= 1. The cited standard results hold for functions in H^k(R^m) or for special extensions, not for the zero extension. The c-example applies (v) to x^dagger in H^2(0,1) with x^dagger >= nu > 0 (nonzero trace) to obtain ||x^dagger_xi - x^dagger||_{L^2} = O(xi^2), which is unsupported and false as derived.

failure_location.quote: For all $s \leq k$ and $\x \in H^k(\Omega_\X)$, $$\norms{\x_\xi-\x}_{H^s} \leq C\xi^{k-s}\norms{\x}_{H^k} = \mathcal{O}(\xi^{k-s})\;.$$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Mollify via a bounded linear extension operator E: H^k(Omega_X) -> H^k(R^m) (x_xi := phi_xi * Ex) instead of the zero extension, or state item (v) only for functions whose zero extension lies in H^k; all stated rates then hold.
issues.overall_effect: The O(xi^2) mollification estimate used for the c-example and the xi-term in the rate eq:xi are unsupported; the balancing between xi, delta and rho_{n xi} rests on a false rate.
issues.title: Mollification rate O(xi^{k-s}) fails for the zero extension
issues.why_classification: A standard local reformulation of the mollifier (extension instead of zero extension) restores every advertised rate with no new proof architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For every $\epsilon > 0$, there exist $\xi > 0$ and a vector $\mathcal{T}_\n$, with associated operator $F_\n$ from \autoref{eq:deeponet}, such that locally uniformly in $L^2(\Omega_\X)$, it holds:

issues.failure_explanation: The prose promises to establish well-definedness of the minimizers of eq:discTikxi, but the following theorem contains only an approximation estimate and no existence argument. Moreover minimizers genuinely need not exist: X_xi = {phi_xi * u : u in L^2(Omega_X)} is the range of a compact, injective convolution operator, hence a proper dense (non-closed) subspace of L^2; e.g. with F_n identically 0 and y^delta = 0 the functional reduces to alpha||x - x^(0)||^2 over X_xi, whose infimum alpha*dist(x^(0), X_xi)^2 is not attained when x^(0) is not in X_xi. The prose thus claims what the paper neither proves nor can hold as posed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: it follows that there exists a $\xi > 0$ such that the following holds locally uniformly within an $L^2(\Omega_\X)$-neighborhood $\mathcal{B}_{\tt r}(\x^*)$  with radius ${ \tt r} > 0$ of $\x^*$:
Therefore, by the Arzel\`a-Ascoli theorem, this subset is compact in $C(\ol{\Omega_\X})$. This compactness satisfies the condition of \autoref{th:operatorapx}.

issues.failure_explanation: Two defects. (i) The proof's first step is a non sequitur: Frechet-differentiability of F gives ||F[x] - F[x_xi|| <= c||x - x_xi|| pointwise in x, and sup over an L2-ball of ||x - x_xi||_L2 does not tend to 0 (functions oscillating at frequency ~1/xi keep ||x_xi - x||_{L2} bounded away from 0), so the claimed locally uniform epsilon/2-bound does not follow; the subsequent Arzela-Ascoli/compactness step controls the wrong set and cannot repair this. (ii) The statement itself is false: F_n from eq:deeponet depends on x only through the finitely many functionals x -> (phi_xi * x)(s_l), whose common kernel is nontrivial in L^2(Omega_X); choosing small smooth h in that kernel with F'[x*]h != 0 (possible for the c-example since y[x*] is not identically 0), both x* and x*+h lie in any ball B_r(x*) and produce identical inputs to F_n, while F[x*+h] - F[x*] is nonzero of order ||h||; hence sup_{x in B_r(x*)} ||F[x] - F_n[x_xi]|| >= c||h|| > epsilon for small epsilon, for every xi and every T_n.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must replace the uniform-over-L2-ball guarantee by one restricted to a family on which both the mollification error and the sample-based neural-operator error can be controlled uniformly (e.g., bounded subsets of H^s, s > m/2), and redo the mollification-error step and the c-example's variational argument under the weakened guarantee.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem thm:l2operatorapx and eq:deeponeterror_l2 are false; the c-example's rate O(sqrt(delta) + sqrt(rho_{n xi}) + xi) (eq:xi), the concluding rate O(sqrt(delta) + xi), and the parameter choices rho_{n xi} ~ delta lose their foundation, so the paper's L^2-theory for the c-example is unsupported.
issues.title: L2-mollification approximation theorem is false; proof's first step is a non sequitur
issues.why_classification: The advertised guarantee type (locally uniform approximation on L2-neighborhoods) is unattainable for operators built from finitely many point evaluations, so no comparable version of the theorem's quantifier structure survives; the advertised L2-regime and the derived rate are lost.
